item.text:
Handoff — correction applied and verified; no external blockers.

Previous result (from [executions/8faf8de3aca1427995e6e6e9b5a79f1e](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-04-05-hashicorp_raft-smoke/executions/8faf8de3aca1427995e6e6e9b5a79f1e/stdout.txt): the exec returned `status: "completed"`, `exit_code: 1`, with

```
=== RUN   TestTCPRoundtrip
    tcp_test.go:14: TCP_OBSERVED request=ping reply=pong
    tcp_test.go:16: TCP_REPLY_ASSERTION: want "wrong", got "pong"
--- FAIL: TestTCPRoundtrip (0.00s)
FAIL	baseline.local/smoke/sample	0.003s
```

That `TCP_REPLY_ASSERTION` failure was expected: the test's own assertion compared the actually-received reply against a hardcoded `"wrong"`. The wiring was functioning correctly — the client sent `ping`, the server read `ping`, and the server wrote `pong`, which the client read back — so the observed pair was `request=ping reply=pong`. The test failed only because `"pong" != "wrong"`, i.e. the assertion deliberately named the wrong literal. The nonzero exit was the test binary's own failure code, not an MCP/service fault.

Change made: a single edit to [sample/tcp_test.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-04-05-hashicorp_raft-smoke/work/sample/tcp_test.go:4), `const wantReply = "wrong"` → `const wantReply = "pong"`. The TCP test body (Listen/Dial/Accept, write `ping`, read, write `pong`, read, log) is untouched; `diff` against the read-only source shows exactly one changed line and nothing else.

New result (from [executions/7c15b9333e024ce9b5830b4ecf766908](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-04-05-hashicorp_raft-smoke/executions/7c15b9333e024ce9b5830b4ecf766908/stdout.txt)): same command, same `cwd`, same 90s timeout, now returns `status: "completed"`, `exit_code: 0`:

```
=== RUN   TestTCPRoundtrip
    tcp_test.go:14: TCP_OBSERVED request=ping reply=pong
--- PASS: TestTCPRoundtrip (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	baseline.local/smoke/sample	0.009s
```

Same observed round trip (`request=ping reply=pong`); the only difference is that the assertion now matches the real reply, so the test passes. As instructed I did not audit the consensus code. note.txt retains the fixture token `context-token-b7b509cdb95b4a349422fc793a5410e2`.
